nesnd_crisis.11.a: Publish the findings and proceed by the usual procedure.
nesnd_crisis.11.d: While checking the chief minister's escort, his guards found a forged order changing the watch. The courier and his accomplices were soon seized by the Embroidered Uniform Guard and the Court of Judicial Review, and held separately according to their rank and part in the plot. The chief minister himself was rushed to a safe place, and returned home only once the culprits were in custody.\n\nThe investigation then spun out of control. It reached officials in key posts handling military procurement and shipping, and these suspects in turn had close dealings with great gentry families of the provinces, and even with the confined lords of the old fiefs. They seemed to hold vital information on several smuggling cases that the Ministry of Justice and the Court of Judicial Review had been quietly examining at the chief minister's request. Yet the Court of Judicial Review and the Embroidered Uniform Guard now disagree on the next step. The cabinet sees a trial by the Court, with the facts laid open to the judicial officers, as a way to begin a large internal inquiry in the open. The Guard insists the matter be kept quiet and investigated in secret, so as not to startle the snake, to lull the traitors and keep the affair from spreading.
nesnd_federal_compact_button: Renew the Compact of the States
nesnd_crisis.30.d: In some districts, after the land commissioners of [ROOT.GetCountry.GetName] went into the countryside with the new law, the military estates still collected rent by the old rules. Farmers who had already paid their redemption price were told by their “masters” that the fields they worked belonged to the military rolls, and that the rent must not be resisted. Several schoolteachers who had written petitions for the farmers were arrested for shielding concealed property.\n\nThe deeds submitted by the counties contradict the garrison registers. The county and provincial authorities want to take over the review, while the commissioners ask the court to send troops to seize the hidden records. As the matter drags on, the farmers who had hoped for land have gathered in their county towns, waiting for an answer from the new government that promised to free them.
ce_cne_land_reform_reason: This movement began with the Western Qin Great Revolution of 1810. People of the age understood it as a modern economic transformation arising among the agrarian states of the East, where powerful lineages had long dominated rural life. Through purchase or compulsory confiscation, land accumulated beyond all measure by its old owners was redistributed among a portion of the peasantry. The aim was to break the lineages' hold over the rural population. The ruling group of the Empire of China suspended the movement during its rise to power. Around Mu Zhongtang's southern campaign of 1820, however, he and his confidants revived it to restore the economy, free productive activity and mobilise peasants and soldiers.
nesnd_federal_compact_button_desc: Now that the full triumph of the new policies can no longer be stopped, events are slipping out of the hands of the Southern Administration in Hangzhou, and that is a good thing! We must therefore rebalance Hangzhou's power against the Western provinces. Just as the old Great Rites Controversy reshaped the Northern Ming state in its middle years, we should seize the present support of the provincial representatives and swiftly convene an extraordinary Great Rites Assembly, the national assembly of Southern Ming, together with a cabinet council. Let them settle anew appointments, tax quotas, military funding and the provincial system, and reorganise our politics on the model of the constitutions and rites of the North, the Western barbarians and Dongzhou. Perhaps then the Zhu sovereign may at last break his shackles and govern the Southern realm.
nesnd_crisis.10.d: The provincial delegates, the members of Southern Ming's parliament, have declared their support for the new laws by a majority in the Great Rites Assembly. The reforms of appointments, land tax and military funding, centred on the central government, have at last been gathered into a widely accepted set of provisions and written into Southern Ming's constitutional “Rites”. Under the new laws, the Ming court, or rather the Ming court as the present regime knows it, has finally drawn the line between the centre and the provinces on the local separatism that has persisted since the Rebellion of the Prince of Sai in the early 15th century of the Western calendar.\n\nAdministrative unity, of course, had been achieved when Chen Dongyang restored the provincial administrative commissions. But that policy never ordered the abolition of the enfeoffed lords, nor fixed the boundary between central and local power. It was only that the Southern and Western Administrations, facing the northern invasion, had stood together as never before, so that no one objected to Nanjing (in truth, Hangzhou) exercising military and civil authority, appointing and dismissing officials, and hunting down those who would not obey. Any who did object were long since ground to dust beneath the iron hooves and iron guns of the two Administrations. Now all these efforts are carved into stone at last, not to be changed for ten thousand generations.
nesnd_crisis.31.d: Field commands everywhere have begun withholding the taxes that should go to the centre. Officers have taken over customs posts, granaries and local offices in the name of feeding their troops, and the land commissioners can only work where the garrisons allow. Unpaid units are demanding estates from their commanders one after another, and the old military blocs have gained wider power over the provinces.\n\nThe redeployment orders issued by [ROOT.GetCountry.GetName] keep coming back unanswered. The court must recognise the powers already held by the commands and the governors if it is to keep the provinces loyal to the centre; if it goes on losing control of army pay and officials, the provinces will set up governments of their own.
nesnd_crisis.32.d: Memorials from the provinces asking for land reform to stop have piled up at court, though they are no more than compromise documents that humiliate the court's ministers and even the Son of Heaven himself. Yet the rulers of [ROOT.GetCountry.GetName] have no choice but to bow to hard realities. Under the proposed compromise, land confirmed by the so-called “new deeds” would remain with the military households, who need only promise their tenants some reduction in rent and not prevent them from leaving to find work elsewhere. Estates, military land and lineage property not yet dealt with would be held by the local authorities as so-called “state public land”, to be let to tenants recruited by the government.\n\nIt would be a humiliation for the court. But if it issues such a decree, the court of [ROOT.GetCountry.GetName] can free the provinces from the endless cycle of surveys, petitions and riots. The local powers organised around the old land rights would also take part once again in collecting taxes and running the villages.
nesnd_crisis.33.d: The arrests that followed the land surveys have brought Shanxi's veterans, local scholars and dispossessed farmers together. Republicans are using village schools and old army ties to pass documents around, calling on every county to elect delegates and put on trial the officers who seized farmland.\n\nHowever, as garrison after garrison refused to hand over the ringleaders, the delegates chosen in the agitation turned to demanding the removal of the chief land commissioner, a fresh review of titles, and compensation for the farmers who were robbed.
nesnd_crisis.20.d: When word came that the Wa-Wu had betrayed Ming and proclaimed their own reign, the ministers north of the river congratulated one another. Some even recalled how the Mu Son of Heaven once rode south in his imperial carriage. After all, the false Wu and their Zheng dogs are too busy fighting the Western provinces to look north. A southern campaign to reunify the realm might succeed at a single stroke.\n\nAt the urging of interested parties, frontier commanders have asked for army funds and sent men to contact the “men of understanding” in Huguang. But our own dynasty is hardly in an age of great peace and prosperity. If land reform is still under way at home, who can say whether joining the Southern melee now will bring fortune or disaster?
nesnd_huguang_preparations_reason: When Zhu Banbo put Huguang in order, he repaired the fortifications of Xiangyang, gathered young officers to teach, and traded military ironware to Sichuan for grain. Wounded and discharged soldiers were assigned to supply services and farming garrisons, and the republicans who stayed in Xiangyang helped the governor-general's office reform Yuelu Academy. In twenty years, the governor-general's army, land revenue and academies grew into one body, and Chen Dongyang backed them at court. Men of the time came to see Xiangyang's troops as the head of the “New Western Administration”, and a pillar without which the Southern Ming federation could not have been founded.\n\nYet the Zheng family, once Zhu Banbo's strongest supporter, now repeatedly accuses Xiangyang at court of withholding taxes and hiding households from the registers. They have also posted away Shi Yuanfu, Lin Hanhan and other senior southern officers close to Huguang, along with many republican officials friendly to us. Every sign says we must prepare for the worst: reassess the soldiers and farming hands of the garrisons, restore grain shipments from upriver, and stir up opinion in the academy to win over the scholars. We must be ready for anything.
nesnd_hna_academy_button_desc: Yuelu Academy in Xiangyang is the spiritual heart of Huguang's officials and its scholars of public affairs. Yet from its founding it has taught a “patriotic” loyalty to the Southern realm. Now, with the Southern Administration striking at us again and again, we must put its staff in order and have Yuelu's teachers, under our direction, gradually teach the difference between the Wa-Wu scum who seize the government and the Zhu Ming imperial house, uniting our own thinking against whatever may come.
nesnd_hna_supply_button_desc: In the recent war against the Mu bandits, Huguang's workshops and Sichuan's grain boats together fed the soldiers and people of Xiangyang. We should reorganise the arms production and grain shipments of the two provinces according to need, and reopen the wartime depots along the river, in case the treacherous ministers strike.
nesnd_hna_veterans_button_desc: Since Zhu Banbo's day, Chu soldiers have been treated far better than their allies in the Southern army. This included fixed terms of service and veterans' assemblies learned from the North, meant to send disciplined, trained veterans to lead farming settlers into the villages and so quickly renew and improve the life of Huguang, long worn down by war. Today the assemblies are well established, and their veterans know both the barracks and the villages. Besides answering the call to mobilise the people in wartime, the assemblies can help us prepare the people economically and in their daily lives.
nesnd_protect_chen_button_desc: The reforms led by Chen Dongyang strike at the estates and titles of gentry everywhere, the old fief-holders of Northern Ming and the officers of the Ming army. Seditious verses and threatening letters are intercepted by our Embroidered Uniform Guard time and again. Chen Dongyang himself may fear nothing, but we can no longer be careless. Given what Master Dongguan, Chen Dongyang, means to the new laws, and to preserve the cabinet's power to press on with reform and the court's drive to centralise, we should choose reliable palace guards and form a dedicated escort to protect Lord Chen.\n\nProtection lasts #v six months#!. Without dedicated guards, the case has death, injury and escape chances of #v 40/25/35#!. Funding and renewal terms appear in the protection proposal.
nesnd_crisis.30.b: Refer the matter to the local consultative bureau.
nesnd_protect_chen_button: Protect the Chief Minister and the Deliberative Process
nesnd_egypt_investment_accounts_reason: Buying machines is easy; keeping the people who can build, repair and run them takes far more effort. The university must turn out our own technical talent, the tool workshops must supply the implements production needs, and the new industries must be able to hire real workers.\n\nThe court hopes these undertakings will become Egypt's own foundation. Wherever the capital comes from, only when there are teachers in the schools and workers in the workshops will the promises on paper have been turned into national strength.
